issue.title: trouble loading the streamlit_ace.ace component
issue.body:
I have a strange problem that occurs randomly.
I have deployed a streamlit app that uses streamlit_ace editor. When I visit the web page, I get the following error
 sometimes and other times it works fine! 
```
Your app is having trouble loading the streamlit_ace.ace component.

(The app is attempting to load the component from **, and hasn't received its "streamlit:componentReady"** message.)

If this is a development build, have you started the dev server?
If this is a release build, have you compiled the frontend?

```

![Screenshot_20201223_165600](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46030335/102991835-0770f980-4540-11eb-814d-5945030420e4.png)
I have it deployed [here](https://back-plt.herokuapp.com/) and [here](https://share.streamlit.io/iamashwin99/back-plt/main/main.py)
It works consistently when run from my laptop with the exact same dependency and versions installed.
here's the output when the app is run locally. 
![Screenshot_20201223_165910](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46030335/102991909-32f3e400-4540-11eb-9a72-15797f18512d.png)

I don't think this is an issue with streamlit-ace, however, I am hoping someone here might recognise the issue and guide me.
If it helps, the source is hosted [here](https://github.com/iamashwin99/back-plt/blob/main/main.py)

body:

issue.title: Add a parameter to set the `COMPONENT_READY` timeout

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
### Problem

First of all, I want to apologize. I'm not sure if this problem is more of a bug or a feature requirement.

On slower devices (older laptop or older smartphone) or a slower network connection, the component will not load due to a three-second timeout. I did not find how to turn off or change the timeout. I only found in the code the constant `COMPONENT_READY_WARNING_TIME_MS`, which is located in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/b4a9f3e2c9f9a56bbc2842fd43150fe4b0bdfcab/frontend/src/components/widgets/CustomComponent/ComponentInstance.tsx#L52

### Solution

**MVP:** Enable `COMPONENT_READY` timeout shutdown or enable timeout change through parameter.

**Possible additions:** The `COMPONENT_READY` timeout could take into account the speed of the device and the speed of the network connection.

### Additional context

I'm not the only one who has encountered this problem. See https://github.com/okld/streamlit-ace/issues/13

body: @erumoico Ah. I see the edits...what are the connection errors you are seeing?

When I start `streamlit run openqa_app.py --server.port 3000` and connect to http://pcknot2.fit.vutbr.cz:3000, than in Firefox console I see:
```
Cross-Origin Request Blocked: The Same Origin Policy disallows reading the remote resource at http://pcknot2.fit.vutbr.cz:8501/healthz. (Reason: CORS header ‘Access-Control-Allow-Origin’ missing).
```
In Chromium:
```
9.59da8a99.chunk.js:2 GET http://pcknot2.fit.vutbr.cz:8501/healthz net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
```

But I think I'm doing it wrong. Because it's an intuitive way, not documented way.

Hmm, interesting. When I connect to http://147.229.13.167:3000 it works. Maybe some trouble with domain name. Or collisions with other streamlit instances. Or something with [CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/CORS).

Both the `streamlit run openqa_app.py --server.port 3000` command and the `yarn start` command from development `streamlit/frontend` directory work.

The `yarn start` command is documented on the [contributing wiki page](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing). Plus, I can increase the [`COMPONENT_READY_WARNING_TIME_MS` constant](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/b4a9f3e2c9f9a56bbc2842fd43150fe4b0bdfcab/frontend/src/components/widgets/CustomComponent/ComponentInstance.tsx#L52). This was necessary because when I have the console running in my browser, the browser is slower and my component often times out.

Now I see the warnings in the browser's console that I expected. After step 6 from [_Steps to reproduce_](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2720#issue-801007381) I see:
```
Warning: Received component message for unregistered ComponentInstance!
Object { isStreamlitMessage: true, type: "streamlit:componentReady", apiVersion: 1 }
```

After step 7, I see:
```
Warning: Received component message for unregistered ComponentInstance!
Object { isStreamlitMessage: true, type: "streamlit:setFrameHeight", height: 357 }
```

Ah gotcha! Good digging @erumoico

By the way, if you download Streamlit from GitHub. Install the dependencies by `make all-devel` You can also do `make package` which generates a wheel file in `lib/dist`. I'm not sure if you have to do a `cd lib; pipenv shell` before that. In any case, you can change that dev flag to true and then use the wheel in the project you deploy and install that. Might be easier than playing with ports at this point 😊

I'm not sure how the custom component isn't showing that it's registered, that's a tougher issue to play with especially for a code example on a deployment 😕
